LEARNING PATH LESSON · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Kind Choice, Good Friend, Try Your Best & Grow Together — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson hands your family growth language: four words that measure the day by growing, not by winning — and a bedtime rewind that collects the evidence.

What is this?

Kind choice, good friend, try your best and grow together are the growing words: the moment you picked kind over easy, the showing-up for someone, the honest effort (not the perfect result) and the getting-bigger that happens side by side.

What does it mean?

Growth language beats cleverness language in every study that compares them: children praised for trying choose harder puzzles; children praised for smart choose easier ones. This card installs the first vocabulary at family scale.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three ideas: kind choice means the pick was yours (nobody made you — that is what makes it strong); try your best is about the TRYING, and best changes day to day (tired-best counts); and grow together means the growing is a WE project — family, friends, everyone.

Why this matters

This card names the arc of the whole class: feelings learned, kindness chosen, and now — growing. It sits before the graduation cards because it gives the family the ruler to measure everything after.

What it teaches

Growth mindset language (process over person), prosocial choice-making (agency), effort attribution, and collective identity — the WE that grows, which is belonging’s twin.

Words to learn

kind choicegood friendtry your bestgrow togethereffortchoicegrowing

Say this to your child

“"In this family we have growing words. Kind choice — when you picked kind even though easy was right there: that was YOURS, you chose it. Good friend — when you showed up: sat with the sad one, waited for the slow one, shared the last one. Try your best — not perfect, just your all; and best is allowed to be tired on Tuesdays. Grow together — because nobody grows alone: we get bigger side by side, you and me and everyone in this house. Those are our words. Not how much, not how fast, not who won — did we grow? We did. Every day, a little."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "The growing words — how we measure a day."
  2. Read the panels: the heart-hugging girl made a KIND CHOICE, the open-armed boy is a GOOD FRIEND, the fist-up boy TRYs HIS BEST, the sprout-cupping girl shows GROW TOGETHER — the only panel holding something alive and small.
  3. Ask the rewind questions (below) at bedtime — growth language installed in ninety seconds.
  4. Retire the word smart for a week: replace every "so clever" with "you worked until it worked" — feel the difference in the child’s posture.
  5. Close with the takeaway: "we do not measure days by winning — we measure them by growing."

Look closer at the picture

On this card four panels hold the growing words: Kind Choice, a girl hugging a heart with closed eyes; Good Friend, a boy with his arms open wide; Try Your Best, a determined boy with a fist up; and Grow Together, a girl cupping a tiny green sprout in her hands — the only card in the class holding a living thing, because that is the point.

Ask your child

"What was today’s kind choice?" "Who did you show up for?" "What did you try your best at — even a tired best?" "What should WE grow tomorrow?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "I made a kind choice!" "I showed up for Sam" or the planner: "tomorrow we grow a bigger tower."

Out in the real world

Growth evidence accumulates quietly: the stair climbed alone (try your best), the truce offered (kind choice), the friend waited for (good friend), the family plant watered (grow together). Name the evidence in passing — the child collects the identity; you just point.

Try it together

The Bedtime Rewind: three questions in the dark, every night: what was today’s kind choice? who was a good friend today (anyone, including you, including a story character)? what did you try your best at? Then one grow-together plan for tomorrow — one seed, chosen together. Ninety seconds, no stickers, no charts — the remembering IS the growing.

Understanding check

Ask: "What makes a kind choice strong? What is try-your-best about — the result or the trying? Who grows alone?" That it is chosen, the trying, nobody — three answers and the family has its ruler.

Parent tips

Guard the word best — best is not perfection, and a tired child’s best is still best; say so out loud or the word starts lying. And when the rewind finds nothing one night (some days are like that), the grown-up donates one: "I saw you pick up the baby’s cup — that was a kind choice." The ruler always finds something when someone else holds it kindly.

This lesson pairs with the Kind Choice, Good Friend, Try Your Best & Grow Together flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Feelings & Kindness (Class 38).
